so bottom line, 
use best engineering practices, 
solid principles, 
latest versions of native android strategy such as kotlin compose 
and only use performant native code 
but support being installed older versions of android as much as possible 
try to not destroy the user's battery 
try to use engineering best practices 
solid principles 
always use latest versions of dependencies 
and latest versions of github actions 
this application will ONLY run on android 
do NOT do any cross platform nonsense like xamarin expo  or whatever 
also this app will NEVER be put on Google Play Store 
so we should support everything Android 12 and above 
why android 12 and above? 
so we can support automatic updates with obtainium and the likes 
if this assumption is incorrect, use your best judgment to support the lowest version of Android possible 
remember, we do not need to support google play store

What the code is

Your repo is upstream Hamza417/Positional at e6fe920 plus export.sh. I used a clone of upstream as the base so the binaries are included.
It’s about 33k lines of Kotlin and Java built on XML views, with no tests.
The 20 MB dump.txt is mostly about 150 res/drawable/launcher_day_* and launcher_night_* vector art files, some over 1 MB each. The code itself is small. I’d add a size cap or exclude rule to export.sh so the dump fits in the project.
Changes done in the sandbox, not yet delivered

Play Store code removed: the license check (licensing/*, AIDL, License, LicenseViewModel, LicenceStatusCallback), the in-app update check in Settings, and the rate card. Settings links now point to your repo and its releases page.
Unused code removed: 20 unreferenced classes, 7 layouts, 12 drawables and the license HTML page.
Comments stripped from every .kt and .java file using a lexer that understands strings. I checked it by running kotlinc 2.4.21 and javac 21 on the code before and after: the error sets were identical and there were no syntax errors.
XML comments: stripping these failed on three HTML assets, which aren’t valid XML. I still need to skip those and re-run.
Findings that shape the build files

android-maps-utils and the google-services classpath are never used, so they’ll be dropped.
The build currently fails outright without a Google Maps key. I’ll make the key optional through an optional MAPS_API_KEY secret. Without it the map stays blank but nothing else breaks.
Latest versions I confirmed on GitHub:
Kotlin 2.4.21 and KSP 2.3.12
Material 1.14.0
checkout v7, setup-java v6, gradle/actions v6, action-gh-release v3
I couldn’t confirm newer AGP or AndroidX versions because Google Maven is blocked from my sandbox. I’ll keep upstream’s (AGP 9.2.1, May 2026) and add Dependabot to raise PRs for anything newer.
I’ll keep the Gradle 9.4.1 wrapper for now: 9.8.2 is out, but I can’t get its checksum from here.
minSdk stays at 24 (Android 7). Obtainium can update any app; only silent updates need Android 12 on the device. There’s no reason to drop older devices.
Compose: rewriting about 33k lines of views is not something I can do responsibly in one pass, and I can’t compile Android code here. I’d do it panel by panel in later turns.
Next turn delivers

A single git rm command covering every removed file.
The whole project as one tar.gz, plus a list of files to delete.
A rewritten app/build.gradle:
signing from your four secrets
versionCode and versionName from the CI run number
optional Maps key
unused dependencies removed
.github/workflows/release.yml: build, unit tests, a signed APK, and a full (non-pre) GitHub release on every push to master.
.github/dependabot.yml.
JUnit 4 unit tests for the pure maths and utility code (math/*, UnitConverter, DMSConverter, and similar).
A new README.
An updated export.sh.

git rm -r --cached .idea
tar -xzf hamza417-positional.tar.gz
git update-index --chmod=+x gradlew export.sh
git add -A && git add --renormalize .
The last git rm keeps your local .idea folder but stops tracking it. The --renormalize step applies the new .gitattributes, which converts every text file to LF line endings, so this first commit’s diff will be large.

What changed
Play Store code removed

The license check and in-app update prompt are gone.
The rate card, its layout block and its preference functions are gone.
The CHECK_LICENSE permission and the Firebase manifest entries are gone.
Settings links now point to your repo and its releases page.
Dead code removed

30 unreferenced classes, 8 layouts, 20 drawables and 6 assets.
SunMoonCalculator and DrawMoonBitmap, which nothing called.
52 unused functions and 39 unused imports.
The unused android-maps-utils and google-services dependencies.
Comments

All comments are stripped from Kotlin, Java, resource XML and the manifest.
Line endings are normalised to LF.
Build

Signing reads KEYSTORE_FILE, STORE_PASSWORD, KEY_ALIAS and KEY_PASSWORD.
VERSION_CODE and VERSION_NAME can be overridden.
The Google Maps key is optional, set through MAPS_API_KEY as a secret or in local.properties. Without it the map stays blank but nothing else breaks.
Dependency metadata is no longer embedded in the APK.
Bumped Kotlin to 2.4.21, KSP to 2.3.12 and Material to 1.14.0.
AGP 9.2.1, AndroidX and the Gradle 9.4.1 wrapper stay as they were, because I couldn’t confirm newer versions from here. Dependabot will open PRs for them.
CI (.github/workflows/build.yml)

Every push and PR runs the unit tests and a debug build.
Each push to master also builds a signed APK, checks the signature with apksigner, and publishes a full release (not a pre-release).
Releases are tagged v1.0.<run number>, with versionCode 20261000 + run number.
Weekly Dependabot PRs cover Gradle dependencies and GitHub Actions.
Tests: 11 test classes (26 tests) cover the math helpers, unit conversion, angles, vectors and quaternions, the compass calculation, the low-pass filter, time-to-angle conversion, and the compass-direction lookup. To make that lookup testable I split it out of Direction.kt as Direction.sector(), which also removes the old gaps where some angles returned “N/A”.

export.sh

The tree lists every file in git.
File contents are written only for source, build, manifest, layout, values and config files.
Binaries, vector art, translations, HTML assets, Room schemas and screenshots are skipped without any marker.
The dump shrinks from about 20 MB to about 1.8 MB.
README: rewritten to cover install via Obtainium, building, the required secrets, CI and the project layout.

Notes
minSdk stays at 24 (Android 7). Obtainium works on older Android too; only silent background updates need Android 12.
The release keeps the applicationId app.simple.positional, so it can’t be installed over the Play Store build of Positional; that has to be uninstalled first.
The original Positional also tells you, in its upstream README, that it uses Google Maps. That remains true here.
